item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM request
Interesting SCP you got here!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

Not gonna lie, I'm digging this idea! A Foundation clone. Or the original foundation that the Foundation was cloned from. who knows? This article is going to be like a dog chasing its tail. Or a tail chasing a dog. It's sure to be a fascinating, mildly infuriating, but nonetheless fun article to see!
You seem to have a solid narrative. Wouldn't it be funny if at the same time SCP was infiltrating the PCS, the PCS was infiltrating the SCP? I kind of like Cybersqyd's idea of having the PCS be an extension of the SCP Foundation and the MTF just raids their own base. Since the two organizations are backronyms of each other, I doubt that such an occurrence could be chalked up to chance. Maybe have some sort of implications or hypotheses to throughout the story? Like the PCS is from an alternate dimension, or both groups are old rivals, or that they're the same organization. Something like that to bring the reader full circle.
I think you have a solid narrative and all. I'm going to just go ahead and give you a tentative greenlight, although I would like you to be a bit more concise with the details. Please feel free to reach out with any questions, and do keep me posted!

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Thanks for getting back to me.

I think I overused the word “exact” in my description here, it should say “similar.” The events are not exactly the same, and it leaves room for a couple of interpretations of what the anomaly actually IS. The second foundation is introduced early on, what I’m going for is for the reader to debate with themselves throughout the article or at the end with whether the PCS Foundation is anomalous, if they’re non-anomalous and have been abusing anomalies to avoid detection, or if NONE of it is anomalous. The SCP Foundation themselves will be having this debate alongside the reader, the addendum will be riddled with Staff Surveys (that the reader can also take) to attempt to get a general consensus on what they believe the PCS foundation to be/be doing so that they can work with certainties, and at the end, our three theories will be proposed in three separate theory documents.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

then recounting an exact replica of the events that occurred at the PCS facility, except it's an interview recounting the exact same events occurring at a SCP facility.

For a second, I thought this was going to lead into the discovery that the two organisations are the same and that there's some kinda anomaly that means some foundation sites aren't recognised as such or w/e.

I think at the end of the day, my core issue with this as a concept can be summarised as 'so what?': the impact of discovering the PCS Foundation, and the question of whether they're actually real, feels very minimal because I'm not really sure what it changes in like, my understanding of what's going on here? Like it feels like it's meant to have a big shocking moment where we realise 'oh! second foundation!' but there's no exploration of the implications of it's existence.

I'm also not necessarily convinced by this as a SCP article: what's the like, description/conprocs about? The PCS foundation? If so, the choice to have the two identical incidents happens feels even weirder because what do they actually like, add to the narrative here beyond reiterating what we already know?

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded: That’s what is gonna be put forth towards the middle-end of the narrative. Theories start getting put forth that maybe there is no anomaly being used by this other foundation but maybe that foundation is itself the anomaly, and that they’ve been hidden for so long because they’ve been employing the same methods as our SCP Foundation to remain hidden from society and all other groups. Historically, they likely didn’t rise in the same way, but their own documentation would disagree. Some things are best left for the reader to speculate about and I think that the beginning of this foundation is one of those things.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
As a point of comparison, you may want to consider SCP-4052. It's not totally similar to your idea, in that the Foundation's rival is decidedly stronger to them in every way, but the point I want to draw is that the rival isn't just a Foundation clone. They're people with sandwich heads, and the reveal that their backronym is the same as the Foundation's is played as a joke at the end.

What's the PCS Foundation's history? If they're not anomalous, why are they and the Foundation so similar down to their backronyms? I'm not getting the sense that this is its own organization which rose to prominence in a similar way to the Foundation.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The SCP refers to a hypothetical anomaly. A new "Foundation," which operates extraordinarily similarly to ours, almost the exact same but for a few differences, which has been clearly operating for years upon years, has suddenly come to our knowledge. Surely, the only way they've been existing for so long without us knowing is if they were using an anomaly to hide themselves… right? Surely, no one matches the Foundation in their ability to hide themselves from the rest of the world…

Right?

Central Narrative: The narrative is going to follow the first encounter between our SCP Foundation, and the PCS Foundation (Process, Condemn, Shield), and then followed up by a MTF exploration of a PCS facility in hunting for the SCP, then recounting an exact replica of the events that occurred at the PCS facility, except it's an interview recounting the exact same events occurring at a SCP facility. By the end, no actual SCP is recovered, or even hinted at existing, hopefully leaving the reader asking if it's possible that just maybe two foundations were so good at hiding that up until now, they hid from each other.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I know theoretical/non-existent SCPs have been done before, but I'm hoping the description here is enough of a hook to keep things going.

Additional Notes: I know I'm not the greatest at summarizations. It may need some.. work. I'd be happy to clarify anything if the need should be there. Additionally, I sort of jumped the gun and wrote up an unfinished draft. If anyone would like, I'd be happy to let you read it, although it needs some heavy revising.
